name: Marcus Reed

five_sec.who_for: People with more money than me
five_sec.trust_why: A pop-up game first thing. Feels like a sales pitch
five_sec.delivers_food_why: HelloFresh boxes in the pop-up and 'Free Meals' at the bottom

full_page.what_stopped_me: Can't see a price without giving my zip. Tiny print says auto-renewing subscription. Recipes have sumac pickles and harissa aioli

HF.quote: Kofta-style tacos with sumac pickles. My kids want nuggets. And I can't see a price without giving my zip.

five_sec.who_for: Moms, looks like. Mom and little girl in the picture
five_sec.next_step: Scroll to see what it costs
five_sec.delivers_food_why: A phone with a list and 'Choose Your Meals'

full_page.what_stopped_me: No price anywhere. 'Try Free for 14 Days' means I pay later. There's a Kid Friendly plan but the food shown is keto and pork chops with rosemary-mustard sauce

EM.quote: 'Kid Friendly' plan sounds right, but the pictures are keto and rosemary-mustard pork chops. And what's it cost? Doesn't say.

five_sec.what_is_it: An app to keep your recipes in
five_sec.who_for: People who already cook a lot
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It's an app for recipes and lists

full_page.what_stopped_me: You bring your own recipes. I don't have recipes. Then it's $5.95 a month

PTE.quote: 'Save recipes while you scroll.' I don't have recipes. That's the whole problem.

five_sec.what_is_it: Plans the week's dinners and the family votes by text
five_sec.who_for: Families where somebody runs the house. Doesn't say mom, which is good
five_sec.trust_why: Says no card needed. Don't know the name
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Green line says 'We don't deliver food'

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's all about the Instacart or Walmart cart and I shop in the store on Saturday. Doesn't say I can just take the list with me. Long page, a lot of reading. The $4.99 Family stuff I don't need
full_page.whats_missing: A line saying you can use the list in the store; one recipe's steps so I know a beginner can do it

DD.quote: Sheet pan chicken tenders, taco night, pasta with hidden veggies. That's food my kids eat and I could cook. $64 for the week, plan's free. I'd try it.

five_sec.next_step: Confused. The button says 'Letter from the CEO'
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Phone says 'Tonight's dinner is a good one' like it's on the way

full_page.whats_missing: A free option that actually plans dinner

OL.quote: Button says 'Letter from the CEO.' I don't want a letter, I want dinner. Then it's $25 a month.

dd_offer.why: Says 'free forever' and also '14 days free'. Two different frees. Had to read it twice
dd_offer.expect_day_15: The texting thing goes away and it stays free.

head_to_head.reason: Free, and the sample week is kid food I can actually cook

EM.reason: Free and shows the dinners; eMeals hides the price

PTE.reason: DinnerDrop gives me the meals; Plan to Eat wants my recipes

HF.reason: Normal food at Walmart prices, no box

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page, under the sample week: 'Shop in the store? Take the list on your phone or print it', plus one recipe's steps shown, so a dad who shops Walmart on Saturday sees it's for him too.
